Taiwan’s Political and Security Future

Michael Hunzeker, Amanda Hsiao, Peter Mattis, and Ryan Evans

November 16, 2026

Taiwan faces mounting questions about its ability to defend itself, a bitter fight over defense spending, and uncertainty about Washington’s commitment to its security. Michael Hunzeker (George Mason University), Amanda Hsiao (RAND), and Peter Mattis (Jamestown Foundation) join Ryan to examine whether Taiwan is preparing fast enough for a possible war, what’s holding up a major U.S. arms package, and whether warmer relations between Washington and Beijing could come at Taipei’s expense. They also turn to Taiwan’s Nov. 28 local elections, where the results could shake up the island’s political landscape and spell trouble for the KMT ahead of the 2028 presidential race.This episode is sponsored by Kibu, which ensures you always know who’s on the other end of every conversation, wherever it happens.
